question.text: What is the relationship between bond prices and market yields?

answer.text: They are inversely related -- when yields rise, bond prices fall, and vice versa
They move in the same direction -- when yields rise, bond prices also rise
There is no relationship between bond prices and yields
Bond prices remain constant regardless of yield changes

explanation.text: The Logic: There is an inverse relationship between yield and bond price. Bond prices tend to be low when market yields are high, and vice versa. The Trap: Option B states the opposite of reality. Options C and D deny the well-established inverse relationship that is fundamental to bond markets. Note: The inverse price-yield relationship is a definitional feature of bond pricing — it holds independently of the specific cause of the yield change.
